title: When, His Salvation Bringing
description: When, His Salvation Bringing in Tonic Solfa to ANGEL'S STORY, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 754 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”, where the book credits them to the S. S. Choir.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens and Sixes Double (7.6.7.6.7.6.7.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ANGEL'S STORY; any other Sevens and Sixes Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: When, his sal-va-tion bring-ing, To Zi-on Je-sus came, The child-ren all stood sing-ing Ho-san-na to his name. Nor did their zeal of-fend him, But, as he rode a-long, He bade them still at-tend him, And smiled to hear their song.

lines: Nor did their zeal offend him,
He bade them still attend him,
And smiled to hear their song.
Though now as king he reigneth
No! while our hearts are tender,
They, too, shall be the Lord's.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ANGEL'S STORY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
